newsitem.title: USA: Muni yields fall 5-10 basis points in past week.
newsitem.headline: Muni yields fall 5-10 basis points in past week.

text.p: Municipal bond yields fell between five and 10 basis points in the week ended Thursday, adding to the prior week's price gains, Delphis Hanover Corp said on Friday.

Thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields were five basis points lower for the second consecutive week, moving to 5.55 percent. Thirty-year Baa yields lost 10 basis points for the second week in a row, dropping to 6.30 percent.
The Treasury long bond over the same period fell 10 basis points, falling to 6.54 percent. It stood at 6.85 percent two weeks ago.
In the intermediate sector, ten-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds shed 10 basis points to 4.80 percent, and Baa-rated muni yields fell five, to 5.60 percent.
Average yields on one-year Aaa-rated and Baa-rated municipal bonds both fell five basis points for the third consecutive week, to 3.60 percent and 4.40 percent, respectively.

The Aaa municipal yield curve was unchanged at 195 basis points for the second consecutive week. The spread between one-year and 30-year Baa's flattened five basis points for the second consecutive week, moving to 190 basis points.

The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was unchanged for the sixth consecutive week at 80 basis points. The 30-year spread narrowed five basis points for the second straight week to 75 basis points.
